thread:
maria: Heads-up — a customer private deployment in eu-west-1 is hitting per-node GPU slot ceilings and performance is degrading. They asked for concise guidance so their edge services can start applying backpressure without a big infra change. :wave:

alex: Short answer: client-side soft admission (local queue + token bucket) + server-side per-customer concurrency caps. Prefer graceful queuing over hard 503s when possible.

sam: Quick checklist we normally give customers:
- limit simultaneous in-flight requests per client (concurrency cap)
- rate-limit token production (tokens/sec + burst)
- local FIFO queue with jittered retry and a max wait window (e.g., 20-60s)
- fallback paths: lower-quality model, stub response, or route to hosted fallback

maria: Can we sketch a tiny example they can paste into their edge service? They want something language-agnostic and a config snippet for envoy/nginx.

jordan: +1. Also call out observability signals to expose so we can help their SRE: gpu_util_pct, pod_slot_free, queue_length, enqueue_rate, dequeue_rate, drop_rate, p95_latency.

lia: Proposed defaults we often suggest for private-tier customers (tune down for smaller GPUs / higher latencies):
- concurrency per customer: 8
- token rate (steady): 20 rps
- burst tokens: 100
- local queue max wait: 30s
- server hard limit: 120s overall request TTL

sam: Example pseudocode (very small):
```python
# token-bucket + concurrency check
if not token_bucket.consume(1):
    # soft path: enqueue locally with jittered retry, return queue position header
    enqueue_local(req, max_wait=30)
else:
    if concurrency_counter.increment_if_below(8):
        call_redwood(req)
        concurrency_counter.decrement()
    else:
        enqueue_local(req, max_wait=30)
```

alex: Envoy config hint: use local rate limit filter + per-connection circuit breaker limits. Example (conceptual):
- local_rate_limit: token-bucket (tokens_per_fill=20, fill_interval=1s, max_tokens=100)
- circuit_breakers: per_host: max_connections=8, max_pending_requests=200

maria: Also recommend a short policy for customers to decide between soft queue vs immediate failure: if their app degrades gracefully with delayed result, queue; if latency hard requirement, return explicit 429 and document fallback.

jordan: Important operational note: queueing increases GPU warm cache reuse which may raise overall GPU utilization and cost. Add guidance: monitor model cache hit ratios and add autoscaling/burst policies before enabling long queues in eu regions with tight quotas.

lia: For private/VPC specifics: network egress isn't the bott in these cases, but watch connection churn and TCP TIME_WAIT when many clients retry aggressively — advise exponential backoff with capped jitter.

sam: Minimal SDK guidance to include in customer docs:
- expose headers: X-Redwood-Queue-Pos, X-Redwood-Est-Wait, X-Redwood-Priority
- support a priority flag so they can mark interactive vs batch

ops-bot: deployment:metrics: queue-latency-alerting created by mara/infra — threshold p95_queue > 5s for 5m

alex: Action items:
- maria: draft a short customer-facing doc with the patterns + envoy/nginx snippets (ETA: EOD tomorrow)
- sam: add Python + Node SDK examples for token-bucket + backoff (ETA: 48h)
- jordan: add alert set and dashboard rows for the suggested signals (ETA: tomorrow)

maria: I'll also add a short section on cost tradeoffs (queue longer = more GPU cycles spent holding warm cache, may push them toward reserved capacity or Dedicated).

lia: One more suggestion: add a small example JSON policy customers can drop into their gateway: keys [concurrency, rate_per_sec, burst, max_wait_s, priority_routes]. That makes it easier for us to parse and offer automated suggestions later.

alex: Looks good. If we keep the doc tight and prescriptive they can implement without touching infra. :+1:

maria: Thanks — I'll post the draft here when ready and ping @jordan for alerts.

sam: FYI, I've seen customers mix token-bucket + leaky-bucket to reduce bursty spikes — may note as an advanced option.

maria: closing notes: keep defaults conservative, recommend monitoring before widening bursts. We'll follow up if the customer opts to enable long local queues (we may need to offer temporary burst capacity).
